paper.title: Efficient learning by implicit exploration in bandit problems with side observations

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-armed bandit problems with side observations (directed observation system)
settings.definition_quote: In each round $t=1,2,\dots,T$, the environment assigns a loss vector $\bloss_t\in[0,1]^\nodes$ for $d$ actions and also selects an observation system described by the directed graph $G_t$. Then ... the learner selects action $I_t$ and subsequently incurs and observes loss $\loss_{t,I_t}$. Furthermore, the learner also observes the losses $\loss_{t,j}$ for all $j$ such that $(I_t \ra j)\in G_t$

unmapped: action set is an arbitrary subset of {0,1}^d with at most m nonzero components (family at_most_m used loosely: S is a subset, not all such vectors)
learner needs per-round approximations of the independence numbers alpha_t of the observability graphs
settings.definition_quote: the learner has access to a possibly huge action set $\Sw\subseteq\ev{0,1}^\nodes$ ... we assume that $\onenorm{\bv}\le m$ ... the relation between the chosen action and the side observations are given by a directed observability graph $G_t$ ... We refer to this feedback scheme as semi-bandit with side observations.

symbols.sum_Q: sum_{t=1}^T Q_t with Q_t = sum_i p_{t,i}/(o_{t,i}+gamma_t) (random; the bound is the expectation of the sqrt)

tuning: eta_t = gamma_t = sqrt(log d/(d + sum_{s<t} Q_s))

source.quote: Assume that for all $t\in[T]$, $\alpha_t/C \le \talpha_t \le \alpha_t \le d$ for some $C>1$, and assume $md>4$. Setting $\eta_ t = \gamma_t = \sqrt{\pa{\log{\nodes} + 1}/\pa{m\pa{\nodes+\sum_{s =1}^{t-1}\talpha_s}}}$, the regret of \fplix satisfies $R_T \le H m^{3/2} \sqrt{\pa{d + C\sum_{t = 1}^{T} \alpha_t}(\log d + 1)}$, where $H$ is $\OO(\log (mdT))$.

results.notes: H is only specified up to O(log(mdT)), so the constant is not exact. Theorem 2 (general bound in terms of the learning rates) is not recorded separately. Requires a linear optimization oracle; expected running time is d times the oracle.
